Apple announces the expansion of its "Supplier Employee Development Fund," a $50 million education programme for workers in its supply chain, with new measures including the establishment of a brand-new Apple education centre in Vietnam.

The country is increasingly becoming an important manufacturing hub, and Apple is gradually diversifying its operations to reduce reliance on China. The centre is being operated in partnership with Hanoi University of Science and Technology (HUST)……

Apple first launched the "Supplier Employee Development Fund" in 2022 in response to concerns about the well-being of workers in its supply chain. The company pledged to invest £50 million and said it plans to focus on both employee education and respect for workers' rights.

The fund's previous work in Vietnam has focused on providing training opportunities for people with disabilities, and the latest development appears to align with an approach rolled out in India earlier this year.

Apple says the programme has so far delivered 9 million training sessions globally, with another 108,000 supply chain employees having taken part in a separate Swift coding course.
